q: Which church is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
n: The UNESCO Baroque Churches of the Philippines (1993) are San Agustin (Manila), Paoay, Santa Maria (Ilocos Sur) and Miag-ao. Manila Cathedral is not on the list. Source: UNESCO (Baroque Churches of the Philippines).

q: Which is the oldest stone church in Manila, its parish founded in 1571?
n: San Agustín Church's parish was founded in 1571, and the present stone church dates from 1607, the oldest in Manila. Source: UNESCO; San Agustin Church Museum.

q: Which is the oldest stone church in Bohol, built by the Jesuits?
n: Baclayon Church (1727), built by the Jesuits, is considered the oldest stone church in Bohol. Source: National Museum of the Philippines (National Cultural Treasure).

q: Which church is the first all-steel church in Asia?
n: San Sebastián Church (1891) is the first all-steel church in Asia. Its prefabricated steel parts, made in Belgium, were assembled in Quiapo, Manila, under engineer Genaro Palacios. Source: NHCP.

q: The National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help, one of Asia's most visited churches, is commonly called:
n: The National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Parañaque is commonly called the Redemptorist or Baclaran Church. Source: Baclaran Church official site.

q: Which church is the seat of the Archdiocese of Manila and the sixth cathedral on its site since 1581?
n: Manila Cathedral, seat of the Archdiocese of Manila, is the sixth cathedral built on its site since 1581. The present building was rebuilt in 1954–58. Source: Manila Cathedral official site.

q: The Minor Basilica of the Holy Child in Cebu City is also called the:
o: Basílica Minore del Santo Niño de Cebú
n: The Minor Basilica of the Holy Child in Cebu City is the Basílica Minore del Santo Niño de Cebú. Source: Basilica del Santo Niño official site.

q: Now the Basilica of the Immaculate Conception, its first builder was Bishop Domingo de Salazar and its present architect Fernando Ocampo. Which church is it?
n: Manila Cathedral (Basilica of the Immaculate Conception) was first built under Bishop Domingo de Salazar. The present building is by Fernando Ocampo (1954–58). Source: Manila Cathedral official site.

q: Which Iloilo church, a 1973 national landmark, has a façade carved with coconut trees and St. Christopher carrying the Child?
n: Miag-ao Church (Santo Tomas de Villanueva) in Iloilo has a facade carved with coconut trees and St. Christopher carrying the Child Jesus. It was a national landmark in 1973 and UNESCO-listed in 1993. Source: UNESCO (Baroque Churches of the Philippines).

q: Which church, first built by the Augustinian Fr. Miguel Murguia, has a huge bell cast from about 70 sacks of donated coins?
n: Panay Church in Capiz, first built by the Augustinian Fr. Miguel Murguia, has one of Asia's largest bells, cast from about 70 sacks of coins donated by townspeople. Source: NHCP; National Museum (National Cultural Treasure).

q: Declared a national landmark in 1973, what is the first all-steel building constructed in the Philippines?
n: San Sebastián Church, declared a national landmark in 1973, is the first all-steel building in the Philippines. Source: NHCP.

q: Which Ilocos Norte church is known for Earthquake Baroque and huge buttresses and is a UNESCO site?
n: Paoay Church in Ilocos Norte is the best-known example of Earthquake Baroque, with massive buttresses, and is a UNESCO site. Source: UNESCO (Baroque Churches of the Philippines).

q: When was the United Architects of the Philippines founded?
n: The United Architects of the Philippines was founded on December 12, 1974, uniting three older architects' organizations. Source: United Architects of the Philippines (official site).

q: In what year was the United Architects of the Philippines (UAP) registered with the SEC?
n: The UAP was organized on December 12, 1974 and registered with the SEC in 1975. It marked its 50th anniversary in 2024–25. Source: United Architects of the Philippines (official history).

q: When was the first UAP president inducted?
n: The first UAP national officers, led by its charter president, were inducted in 1975 after the December 1974 founding. Source: United Architects of the Philippines (official history).

q: Who was the first Charter President of UAP in 1975?
n: Ar. Norberto M. Nuke served as the first (charter) national president of the UAP in 1975. Source: United Architects of the Philippines (past national presidents).

q: Who was the first woman president of both the UAP and ARCASIA?
n: Ar. Yolanda David-Reyes was the first woman national president of the UAP and the first woman president of ARCASIA (Architects Regional Council Asia). Source: UAP; ARCASIA past presidents.

q: Who was the first president of the Philippine Architects Society (later renamed Philippine Institute of Architects — PIA)?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was the first president of the Philippine Architects Society (1933), later renamed the Philippine Institute of Architects. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Nakpil); UAP history.

q: Besides the LPA and APGA, which group joined to form the UAP?
n: The UAP was formed from three groups: the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA), the League of Philippine Architects (LPA) and the Association of Philippine Government Architects (APGA). Source: United Architects of the Philippines (official history).

q: Which UAP award honors outstanding Filipino architects?
n: The UAP Likha Gold Medal is the UAP's highest award for outstanding Filipino architects. Source: United Architects of the Philippines (awards).

q: What was the National Museum of Fine Arts building originally?
n: The National Museum of Fine Arts building was originally the Legislative Building (Old Congress Building). Source: National Museum of the Philippines.

q: Who was the Filipino architect responsible for the design of the building now known as the National Museum?
n: Juan Arellano, with Antonio Toledo, redesigned and completed the Legislative Building (1926), now the National Museum of Fine Arts. Source: National Museum of the Philippines; NHCP.

q: Under the Burnham Plan, what was the building now housing the National Museum meant to be?
n: In Burnham's 1905 plan for Manila, the building now housing the National Museum was meant to be the National Library. Its use changed to the Legislative Building during design. Source: National Museum of the Philippines (building history).

q: In 2015, the National Museum underwent major renovation works under which architectural firm?
n: The 2015–2018 restoration of the National Museum buildings was carried out with Galicia Architects as heritage architect. Source: National Museum of the Philippines (restoration reports).

q: What is the name of the central theme of the renovation and retrofitting works done at the National Museum?
n: "Tree of Life" was the central theme of the National Museum renovation and retrofit, expressed in the courtyard's skylight and sculpture. Source: National Museum of the Philippines.

q: The Coconut Palace by Francisco Mañosa is also called:
n: Francisco Mañosa's Coconut Palace is also called Tahanang Pilipino ("Filipino Home"). It is built largely of coconut materials. Source: NCCA (Mañosa); Coconut Palace history.

q: What is the dominant shape of the floor plan of Tahanang Pilipino, resembling a sliced coconut when served?
n: The Coconut Palace's floor plan is octagonal, and its roof recalls a sliced coconut or a salakot. Source: Coconut Palace history; Mañosa & Co.

q: Who was the architect of the church known as Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage in Antipolo?
n: José L. de Ocampo designed the present Antipolo Cathedral (National Shrine of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage), completed in 1954. Source: Antipolo Cathedral history; CBCP.

q: Who is the architect behind the art and sports center located in San Juan, Manila?
n: JAGNUS Design Studio designed the art and sports center in San Juan, Metro Manila. Source: JAGNUS Design Studio project page.

q: What is the name of the development in San Juan designed by JAGNUS Design Studio that combines art, retail, and sports?
n: The RONAC Art Center in San Juan, by JAGNUS Design Studio, combines an art gallery, retail and a sports facility. Source: JAGNUS Design Studio; RONAC Art Center.

q: What style is the Manila Cathedral?
n: The present Manila Cathedral (1954–58, by Fernando Ocampo) is Neo-Romanesque. Source: Manila Cathedral official site.

q: Manila Cathedral is dedicated to:
n: Manila Cathedral is the Minor Basilica and Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception. Source: Manila Cathedral official site.

q: When was the last major retrofit of Manila Cathedral completed?
n: Manila Cathedral's last major seismic retrofit and restoration (2012–14) was completed with its reopening in April 2014. Source: Manila Cathedral official site; news reports April 2014.

q: The Grand Mosque in Cotabato was a gift from His Highness, the Sultan of Brunei, to the people of Cotabato. Who was the architect of this structure?
n: Palafox and Associates designed the Grand Mosque of Cotabato (Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah Masjid), a gift of the Sultan of Brunei completed in 2011. Source: Palafox Associates project page.

q: What color are the domes of the Grand Mosque in Cotabato?
n: The Grand Mosque of Cotabato is known for its gold-coloured domes. Source: Palafox Associates; Philippine news reports.

q: The church known as the Basilica Minore del Santo Nifio is primarily constructed from which type of stone?
n: The Basilica del Santo Niño in Cebu is built of coral (Mactan) stone, a limestone quarried from Mactan Island. Source: Basilica del Santo Niño official site; National Museum.

q: What is the oldest documented house in the Philippines, in Cebu City?
n: The Jesuit House (Casa de los Jesuitas, 1730) in Parian, Cebu City is the oldest documented house in the Philippines. Source: Jesuit House 1730 museum; NHCP.

q: When was the Jesuit House in Cebu City built?
n: The Jesuit House in Cebu City is dated 1730 by an inscription on its structure. Source: Jesuit House 1730 museum.

q: What is the large church on the Ateneo de Manila campus?
n: The Church of the Gesù (2002) is the large church on the Ateneo de Manila campus. Source: Ateneo de Manila University.

q: Who designed the Church of the Gesù at Ateneo?
n: The Church of the Gesù at Ateneo was designed by Recio + Casas (Jose Pedro Recio and Carmelo Casas). Source: Ateneo de Manila University; Recio + Casas.
